rounds.text: Gujarat Kidney & Super Speciality Ltd is backed by exceptional top-line and bottom-line expansion, demonstrated by a compounded sales growth of 154% over the trailing twelve months and a staggering three-year compounded profit growth of 1058% [E14, E15]. This phenomenal operating momentum is reinforced by a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100, which highlights massive year-on-year sales growth of 195% and net profit growth of 129% [E50, E51, E53]. The company benefits directly from a robust healthcare sector tailwind with a score of +0.67, significantly outperforming sector medians where sales growth sits at 19.2% and profit growth at 17.3% [E59, E60, E61]. Furthermore, the balance sheet remains exceptionally secure, featuring a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.11x and a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 3.76x [E26, E27]. Market participation also reflects underlying strength, evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, a high Sharpe ratio of 1.69, and positive institutional money flow [E33, E40, E43]. Conceded: the valuation is rich with a P/E of 65.6x, a discounted cash flow valuation pointing to overvaluation, and negative operating and free cash flows in March 2026 [E1, E23, E25, E35].

Gujarat Kidney & Super Speciality Ltd currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E ratio of 75.35x compared to a sector benchmark of 30.5x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 43.99x against a sector benchmark of 16.42x [E11]. This aggressive pricing is further challenged by a discounted cash flow analysis that suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 103 per share, implying a margin of safety of -53.0% [E34, E35]. Operational efficiency is deteriorating, as evidenced by a decline in operating margins from 41% to 25% over three years [E19] and a negative cash conversion of -0.24x [E23]. The company’s working capital cycle has worsened, with days increasing from 55.7 to 91.1 [E49], while debtors remain high at 172 days [E48]. Furthermore, institutional confidence appears to be waning, as foreign and domestic institutional holdings have declined by 3.95 and 1.42 percentage points respectively since December 2025 [E31, E32]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong growth metrics, including 154% compounded sales growth and 1058% compounded profit growth over three years [E14, E15].

The bear’s focus on valuation metrics like P/E and EV/EBITDA [E6, E11] ignores the reality that high-growth companies command premiums; GKSL is currently delivering exceptional compounded sales growth of 154% [E14] and profit growth of 1058% over three years [E15], which fundamentally justifies a higher multiple than stagnant sector peers. While the bear cites a DCF valuation [E34, E35], this model is a static snapshot that fails to account for the company’s current momentum, evidenced by a 100 relative-strength rating against the Nifty 500 [E40] and a positive institutional money flow signal [E33]. Conceded: the company is not paying dividends [E4, E47] and operating margins have declined [E19, E20]. However, the bear’s critique of institutional holdings overlooks the fact that the company maintains a strong, stable promoter stake of 71.45% [E30], and the business is supported by a clear healthcare sector tailwind [E57, E59]. Furthermore, the concern regarding working capital [E49] and cash flow [E23, E24] must be weighed against the company’s conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.11x [E26] and comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 3.76x [E27]. Finally, the market’s confidence is reflected in the stock’s strong Sharpe ratio of 1.69 [E43] and the fact that it is currently expected to deliver a good quarter [E46].

Conceded: the company demonstrates strong sales growth [E14, E51, E52]. However, the bull's dismissal of valuation metrics as mere proof of a high-growth premium ignores that the stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 75.35x against a sector benchmark of 30.5x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 43.99x versus a 16.42x sector median [E11]. While the bull dismisses the DCF model as a static snapshot, a reverse DCF reveals that today's price already aggressively prices in 23.9% earnings growth, surpassing the base case of 18.0% [E36]. The bull cites positive institutional money flow [E33], but overlooks the concrete exit of smart money, with foreign institutional holdings plunging from 10.47% to 6.52% and domestic institutions falling from 1.67% to 0.25% [E31, E32]. The bull highlights stable promoter stakes [E30] and liquidity [E26, E27] to offset cash flow concerns, but omits that operating cash flow is negative at Rs -4 Cr and free cash flow sits at an alarming Rs -98 Cr [E24, E25]. Finally, the bull's reliance on high momentum ignores severe operational degradation, evidenced by operating margins collapsing 16 percentage points over three years alongside chronic high debtors of 172 days and surging working capital days [E19, E48, E49].
